title: 第16章：再遇苏雨琪
novel_title: 穿越两界，我在80年代当倒爷
content_zh:
“老板，一样给我来20斤。”

    马超压下心底翻涌的狂喜，对着老板报了一个他以前连想都不敢想的数量。

    “没问题！”

    老板痛快装袋，然后忍不住问：“小孩，这些可不轻，你咋拿回去？你家大人呢，没跟你一块过来？”

    马超笑了笑：“就我一个，老板你放心就行，我力气大着呢，这点东西难不倒我。”

    他经历过前世吃苦打拼，又常年干农活，身体素质远超寻常同龄人，四十斤粮食对他来说，确实不算什么重担。

    老板见他说得自信笃定，不像是逞强吹牛，便不再多问，手脚麻利地装米装面，按照活动折扣算好了价格。

    马超付完钱，看着脚下两袋沉甸甸的米面，心里稳得不行。

    这一批货带回八零年初的老家，绝对是稳赚不赔的硬通货，不仅能彻底改善家里的伙食，还能帮他攒下真正的启动资金。

    他没急着走，转头看向老板，开口问道：“老板，我再问一下，这附近哪里有卖布料的地方？”

    老板闻言微微一愣，有点意外地打量了他一眼。

    这年头年轻人大多不爱逛布料店，一个半大孩子买完米面又问布料，属实少见。
content_en:
"Boss, give me the same 20 pounds."

    Ma Chao suppressed the ecstasy in his heart and reported an amount to his boss that he had never dared to think of before.

    "No problem!"

    The boss packed the bags happily, and then couldn't help but ask: "Kid, these are not light, how can you take them back? Where are your adults, they didn't come with you?"

    Ma Chao smiled: "It's just me, boss, just don't worry, I'm very strong, this thing won't trouble me."

    He had experienced hardship and hard work in his previous life, and had been doing farm work all year round. His physical fitness was far superior to that of ordinary people of his age. Forty pounds of grain was indeed not a heavy burden for him.

    When the boss saw that he was speaking confidently and not like he was bragging, he stopped asking any more questions, packed the rice and noodles quickly, and calculated the price based on the event discount.

    After Ma Chao paid the money, he looked at the two heavy bags of rice noodles at his feet and felt extremely calm.

    This batch of goods was brought back to his hometown in the early 1980s. It was definitely hard currency that was sure to make a profit. It would not only completely improve the family's food, but also help him save real start-up capital.

    He didn't leave in a hurry. He turned to look at the boss and asked, "Boss, let me ask again, where is the place that sells fabrics nearby?"

    The boss was slightly startled when he heard this, and looked at him a little surprised.

    These days, most young people don't like to visit fabric stores. It's really rare for a half-year-old child to ask about fabrics after buying rice and noodles.
